messages:
sara: Quick follow-up to the ensemble routing RFC — had a few operational concerns after the spike tests yesterday. TL;DR: we need a safer fallback path for dashboard queries that minimizes RBAC re-eval work and keeps latency SLOs.

matt: can you summarize the worst-case? was it auth scoring or the multiplexer?

sara: multiplexer + RBAC fanout. When ensemble tries 3 backends (tile-cache, small-render, full-render) we ended up touching the auth service 3x per request for edge tokens. CPU + latency stacked.

jamie: ouch. we assumed auth cache would absorb that. looks like the cache TTL and hit rate are the weak link.

ashley: two quick ideas: 1) push prefilter auth decisions into the gateway (token->capability map) so we can short-circuit most tenants, 2) attach auth proof to cached tiles so reading cache doesn't re-eval. both are invasive though.

matt: +1 on attaching auth to tiles. that means cache key grows but avoids remote calls. what's the eviction/ttl impact?

sara: we measured yesterday: attaching a signed capability (short-lived) to tiles increases cache size ~6% but cuts auth calls >80% in the happy path. worst-case still needs fallback.

jamie: for the multiplexer itself, can we change the routing to sequential-degrade instead of parallel fanout? do small-render first, only if miss then full-render. saves work but costs slightly higher p95 for cold misses.

ashley: sequential makes sense for typical queries. For SLA-critical routes we keep parallel hedging. We need a per-route policy.

matt: policy per-route + canary rollout. also add metrics: auth_calls_per_req, cache_signed_tile_hit, sequential_fallback_rate. we should gate rollout behind those.

infra-bot: deploy: canary named "ensemble-auth-cache-v1" queued for staging at 2026-03-30T16:00Z (job #4321).

sara: action items: (1) jamie to prototype sequential-degrade switch behind config flag (ETA 3d), (2) ashley to sketch signed-capability-with-ttl for tiles and storage implications (ETA 4d), (3) matt to add telemetry + SLO guards to mux (ETA 2d). i'll update the RFC with these tradeoffs and a cutover playbook.

jamie: i can also add a small e2e test that simulates TTL churn and measures auth call counts.

ashley: remember to include the security review for capability propagation — we need key rotation and short TTL design spelled out.

matt: will do. also recommend a gradual ramp with a hard rollback if auth_calls_per_req increases >5x or p99 latency regresses >15%.

sara: perfect. i'm scheduling a 30m follow-up sync tomorrow 10:30 to walk the playbook and cutover checklist. tagging @matt @jamie @ashley.

matt: :thumbsup:

jamie: ack

infra-bot: meeting created: "Ensemble routing cutover sync" 2026-03-31T10:30Z. Calendar invite sent to participants.
